subject: SLO evidence acceptance pack and measurement checklist for FunCorp RFP
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@funcorp.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: procureops@funcorp.com, techops@funcorp.com
Date: 2026-11-20T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: RFP question: acceptable SLO evidence and sample telemetry

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. Our procurement team (cc'ed) and TechOps are finalizing the SLO validation gate for internal sign-off. Two quick asks so we can close the evidence checklist: 1) what specific telemetry artifacts do you consider "authoritative" for uptime and p99 latency; and 2) can you provide a sanitized sample set (logs/metrics) we can ingest into our verifier so our automation can reproduce the measurement?

We're looking to avoid open-ended evidence requests — an explicit, small set of files and a short acceptance checklist would help legal and engineering move faster. If you already have a template acceptance package that customers have used in prior procurements, please send it over.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
FunCorp
From: soojin.lee@redwood.com <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@funcorp.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-23T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP question: acceptable SLO evidence and sample telemetry

Hi Alyssa — great question and thank you for the clarity on your verification needs. We've put together a compact "SLO evidence acceptance pack" that we regularly provide for enterprise RFPs; attached is a sanitized sample and a short README. High level:

- Authoritative artifacts we provide: 1) aggregated service telemetry (1-minute prom-style counters and histograms), 2) request-level traces for representative windows (partial traces with request id, start/end timestamps, model variant, region), and 3) raw ingestion probe ping logs for synthetic coverage.
- Measurement recipe: our playbook shows the exact queries used to derive uptime and p99-latency (PromQL and SQL for stored aggregates), the windowing rules (UTC, 30-day rolling windows unless you request a vendor-specific window), and alignment rules for cross-region weighting.
- Sanctions and redaction: the sample telemetry in the attached zip is anonymized (no customer ids) and includes trace ids that map only to synthetic probes.

Attachments: funcorp-slo-evidence-README.pdf (short checklist), telemetry-sample-202611.zip (sanitized artifacts), slo-measurement-playbook.md (detailed queries and runbook).

I'll summarize acceptance criteria inline below to make it easy for your automation to validate. If you want, Karthik can join a short call next week to walk TechOps through the playbook and the queries.

Acceptance checklist (short):
- Presence: three artifact types above present in top-level zip.
- Time sync: traces and counters include ISO timestamps and timezone (UTC) and the README documents clock-sync assumption.
- Query parity: PromQL/SQL used by FunCorp verifier returns the same bucket counts for a 24-hour sample window (tolerance for sampling bias <= 1%).
- p99 definition: end-to-end server-side latency measured at the gateway-to-tokenize boundary (documented in playbook).
- Uptime definition: traffic-weighted successful requests / total requests with explicit retries excluded per the playbook.

Next steps: if this checklist looks good, we'll drop a Drive folder with the full pack and open a short (30m) walk-through with Karthik and your TechOps.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP question: acceptable SLO evidence and sample telemetry

Folks — adding the technical detail Alyssa asked for so FunCorp's verifier can be deterministic. I'm attaching an excerpt from the playbook (also in the pack) but key points below:

- Telemetry schema: counters (request_total, request_success_total), histograms (latency_bucket with explicit boundaries), and trace spans include attributes: span.kind, service.name, model.variant, region, request.id. The sample zip includes CSV exports that map to these.
- Windowing and alignment: compute p99 over non-overlapping 5-minute buckets, then compute a weighted p99 over the 24-hour window using request_total as weights. This avoids percentile distortions from variable QPS. Examples and reference PromQL are in slo-measurement-playbook.md.
- Clock sync guidance: we recommend NTP-synced UTC and provide an offset-correction query for cases where customer clocks deviate by <150ms. If offsets exceed that, we include guidance on re-aligning traces via server-side timestamps.
- Failure exclusion rules: documented rules for excluding maintenance windows, DDoS mitigation events, and traffic spikes caused by customer-side misconfiguration. Those exclusions are annotated in the evidence bundle with a short reasoning note.

Alyssa — if your automation needs example PromQL assertions we can commit to a small set of assertion files (we've done this before for other customers). Sending the high-level details here so legal has the compact description they requested.

-Karthik
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Alyssa — attaching the Drive link and a short checklist for your verifier team. We've included two small assertion files your harness can run: promql-assertions.txt and p99-assertions.sql.

Summary of what we uploaded to the Drive folder:
- funcorp-slo-evidence-README.pdf: one-page checklist (what to look for, run order).
- telemetry-sample-202611.zip: CSV exports (counters, histograms), 50 sanitized spans (JSONL), and a small synthetic probe log.
- slo-measurement-playbook.md: measurement recipe, PromQL/SQL examples, windowing and exclusion rules.
- promql-assertions.txt and p99-assertions.sql: machine-readable assertions your automation can run; they return PASS/FAIL for the sample window.

Would you like us to provision a temporary service-account with read-only access to the Drive folder for your verifier, or would you prefer the zip delivered via SFTP? Also happy to do a 30-minute run-through with TechOps; Karthik is available Dec 3rd or 4th in the morning Pacific.

If everything passes your verifier, we can mark SLO-evidence acceptance as complete for procurement and surface the result where your legal team expects it.

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing this.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
